name: Media
scope: Established media institutions across all formats — newspapers, wire services, broadcast/current-affairs TV, radio, institutional and mass-distribution podcasts, documentary producers, studios and streaming platforms.
excludes: Isolated social-media posts, user-generated commentary, self-published advocacy without institutional production; and the government statements / scientific papers / hearings themselves (reporting on them is a Media act). Fiction counts only for cultural legibility, never as factual evidence.
method: First-principles ladder ordered by institutional cost, editorial control, factual responsibility, reputational exposure, continuity and difficulty of reversal. Audience size is not the ordering principle. Non-ontological. Measures possibility of exposure, not causal persuasion.
read: Far past newspapers — investigations, prime-time, podcasts, documentaries, streaming, fiction. Access and visibility are solved; what is missing is permanence and accountability that outlast individual personalities.
summary: Media disclosure has progressed far beyond newspapers: UAP now appears in elite investigations, prime-time TV, mass podcasts, premium documentaries, global streaming and studio fiction. The frontier is no longer access or visibility, but institutional permanence and epistemic accountability — the ecosystem remains uneven, personality-dependent and poorly standardized despite broad mainstream reach.
sourcingQuality: Strong — first-party media artifacts (articles, episodes, platform pages, corporate appointments, audience reports). One 2026 fiction film is post-cutoff, taken from source + confirmation.

rungs.title: Mainstream cultural legibility
rungs.oneLiner: Fiction makes UAP a legible cultural subject. e.g. Close Encounters; Amblin 2026.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Fiction/entertainment make contact, secrecy and disclosure widely recognizable cultural concepts. Lowest rung — familiarity, not factual platforming.
rungs.statusRationale: The subject is a widely recognizable cultural concept. Fiction counts ONLY here, never for evidence or investigation.

sources.label: Close Encounters of the Third Kind — National Film Registry

rungs.title: Factual mass platforming
rungs.oneLiner: A mass platform lets real witnesses make claims. e.g. JRE #1361 (Fravor), Spotify.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A mass platform gives real witnesses/officials extended direct access to make UAP truth-claims. Real people under their own names, above fiction, below verification.
rungs.statusRationale: Extended mainstream platforming of a first-hand military witness is demonstrated. Measures access, not verification.

sources.label: The Joe Rogan Experience #1361 (Cmdr David Fravor), Oct 2019 — Spotify distribution
sources.note: platform distribution, not an editorial finding

rungs.title: Commissioned nonfiction treatment
rungs.oneLiner: An institution funds a factual programme. e.g. CBS 60 Minutes 2021; Netflix Encounters.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A recognized institution commits production resources to a structured factual programme/series.
rungs.statusRationale: Major institutions have commissioned and broadcast serious factual UAP programming. Production commitment, not evidentiary reliability (that is rungs 4-5).

rungs.title: Original evidence-building investigation
rungs.oneLiner: A newsroom builds an original account. e.g. NYT 2017; New Yorker 2021.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A newsroom independently gathers records, develops sources and builds an original account, exposing itself to correction and legal scrutiny.
rungs.statusRationale: An elite newsroom committed its reporting machinery to an original national-security investigation. Threshold crossed.

sources.label: NYT, Glowing Auras and 'Black Money', 16 Dec 2017

rungs.title: Adversarial verification & narrative plurality
rungs.oneLiner: Outlets test claims, publish competing findings. e.g. WIRED 2018; WSJ 2025.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Outlets independently test source chains, images and official explanations, publishing findings that can contradict advocates AND government.
rungs.statusRationale: Major outlets have published competing, mutually challenging accounts. Adversarial journalism exists — not final adjudication.

sources.label: WIRED video-provenance investigation, Feb 2018 (self-corrected a technical point)

rungs.title: Recurrent multi-format programming
rungs.oneLiner: Repeated commissioning across formats. Partial: event-triggered, few producers.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Repeated commissioning/distribution across years and more than one factual format.
rungs.statusRationale: Real recurrence exists (Nat Geo two seasons, Netflix slate, Showtime, Prime Video), but substantial gains remain in continuity, producer diversity, depth, fact-checking and non-English production. Highly reversible.

sources.label: Nat Geo, UFOs: Investigating the Unknown, S1 (2023) + S2 (2025)

rungs.title: Dedicated institutional ownership
rungs.oneLiner: Named staff/programme own the beat. Partial: NewsNation/Coulthart, one-correspondent-dependent.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A company assigns identifiable staff / a recurring programme / a unit with continuing responsibility.
rungs.statusRationale: NewsNation formally assigned a correspondent and a recurring programme, but it is one-correspondent-dependent, not a permanent multi-person UAP desk, with no published succession.

sources.label: Nexstar hires Ross Coulthart as NewsNation special correspondent, Nov 2023

rungs.title: Cross-platform mainstream normalization
rungs.oneLiner: Present across news, podcast, streaming, doc, fiction. Partial: reversible, tied to news cycles.
rungs.firstPrinciples: UAP treated as a recurring, intelligible subject across news, broadcast, podcast, documentary, streaming and fiction — not one format or a fringe channel.
rungs.statusRationale: Cross-platform presence is achieved; cross-platform maturity is not. News remains event-triggered, long-form leans on a few guests, quality is uneven, and the subject can revert to spectacle.

sources.label: Combined record across CBS, Spotify, Netflix, Nat Geo, Prime Video, major papers, NewsNation (rungs 1-7)

rungs.title: Accountable, successor-proof institutionalization
rungs.oneLiner: No durable desks, provenance rules, labeling, or standards outlasting individuals.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Engagement survives personalities and news cycles — durable desks, transparent provenance, consistent corrections, clear genre labeling, stable commissioning, professional recognition.
rungs.statusRationale: No qualifying public evidence of such an integrated architecture applied consistently to UAP's specific problems (unverifiable classified claims, imagery provenance, genre boundaries).

excludedClaims.claim: "The tone has shifted / less mockery / the media has turned"
excludedClaims.reason: Real but impressionistic — not a datable, sourceable editorial act. Audience figures show reach, not persuasion.
An individual act, not an institutional newsroom decision; lives outside the ladder.

excludedClaims.claim: An advocacy group uploading its own film
excludedClaims.reason: Not institutional media engagement; a major platform commissioning/distributing it would be.

crossTrackNotes: A Pentagon release is Government; CBS/Netflix deciding how to report it is Media. A hearing is Legislative; its broadcast/fact-check is Media. A Villarroel paper is Scientific; a Nat Geo episode explaining it is Media. Fiction stays at cultural-legibility/normalization only.
